page.overview:
What is potions?

A potion (Latin potio, 'beverage') or elixir was a magical mixture, commonly brewed in a cauldron, which was used to create a number of magical effects on the drinker. Potions ranged in effects, nature, and brewing difficulty. All potions required some wandwork and a spell to be successfully completed when brewed.

An example of a beginners potion was the Cure for Boils, which was the first potion learned at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry. An incredibly advanced and challenging one was the Polyjuice Potion, that even adult witches and wizards had trouble with.

A wizard or witch who specialised in potion brewing was known as a potioneer

Notably, the potion-making of Native American witches and wizards was more advanced with a higher degree of complexity and sophistication than in European countries.
